summary: Concrete ObjectGenome next-depth leaf: support-cycle validation still uses recursive DFS over an otherwise unbounded component graph, so a sufficiently deep plain acyclic support chain can turn fail-closed recipe inspection into a Luau stack failure. Preserve the accepted recipe surface by replacing the recursive cycle walk with iterative tri-color DFS and add a deterministic long-chain adversarial regression.
evidence: src/shared/Objects/ObjectGenome.luau validates components as a dense array with no explicit component-count or support-depth ceiling, then detects support cycles through a recursive local visit(componentKey) call for each support edge.
The same validator already uses an explicit iterative stack for support-to-ground reachability, showing the contract does not require recursive graph traversal.
tests/object_genome.luau covers small cycles, grounded cycles, branched cycles, ground-reachable cycles, and component-order invariance, but has no deep-chain/stack-safety regression.
Repository PR search found no ObjectGenome support-cycle recursion/stack hardening PR; active primary #318 addresses familyVersion and state/registry aliasing instead.

Implementation should first capture the smallest practical failing chain length under the canonical Lune runner, then lock a comfortably deep deterministic regression. Do not add a new component-count limit unless a measured budget/contract decision separately requires one.
